long_biography.plain_text:
Vladimir Sergeyevich Lisin began working as an electrical fitter at a Siberian coal mine while studying metallurgy. He moved into steelmaking at Tulachermet, advancing from assistant steelmaker to deputy shop manager, then held engineering and executive posts at the Karaganda Steel Plant. Work with Trans World Group placed him on the boards of major metals producers and led to a shareholding in NLMK.

Lisin joined NLMK's board in 1996 and became chairman two years later, ultimately securing control of the steelmaker. He also assembled a transport platform around ports, shipping and freight rail, retaining Port One after selling Freight One. He also pursued technical and economic research, authoring metallurgical studies and receiving numerous patents for metals-production processes.
